newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown -- text of statement on NAO report.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown -- text of statement on NAO report.

text.p: Following is the text of a statement by British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown, released by the Treasury, on a report by the National Audit Office. BUILDING BUDGETS ON HONEST AND OPEN FOUNDATIONS
The Head of the National Audit Office today endorsed the Chancellor's new assumptions for forecasting public finances.
In welcoming the independent report from Sir John Bourn, the Comptroller and Auditor General of the NAO, Gordon Brown commented:
"Budgets must be built on honest foundations. This is the only way to restore public trust in the public finances.

"This is the first time that any Chancellor has opened up the Treasury's forecasting assumptions to such open and independent scrutiny. And it means that the Budget arithmetic will be based on financial conventions which are open, transparent and accountable.

"I am delighted that the National Audit Office have provided independent backing for my new assumptions for forecasting public finances. The NAO note that the assumptions have been arrived at systematically on the basis of the available data and by methods which interpret it in a reasonable way.'
-- not to anticipate any privatisation proceeds after the current year is reasonable;

-- on the main elements of Spend to Save, the deterrent effects could...reasonably be excluded from the estimated savings... (Inland Revenue projections) and ...reasonably be omitted (Customs and Excise projections);
-- underlying growth of the economy at 2 1/4 per cent ... would seem broadly consistent with past experience...and with assessments of the medium-term prospects for growth
-- as a level assumption for claimant unemployment...the figure seems consistent with the available independent assessments
-- using financial market information...is a reasonable way of setting assumptions about interest rates for the purposes of fiscal projections

"Together with the action we are taking against fraud, waste and mismanagement, such as earlier this week in Europe and today in the NHS, this audit demonstrates our clear intention to put the public finances on the soundest long term footing."
"I intend that, as part of the opening up of economic decision making which I believe is right, there should be a continuing role for the National Audit Office in subsequent Budgets."
